subject: Aperture - AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: billing mapping questions
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire@aperture.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace integration questions + sample invoice

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Aperture is excited to move toward an AWS Marketplace listing. Our procurement team needs to validate how metering + fulfillment will appear on our invoices and how entitlements map back to our internal SKUs.

Quick asks to help unblock procurement:
- Can you confirm whether usage will be billed through AWS (Marketplace meter) or directly via Redwood for our first-year contract?
- We need a sample invoice that shows line-item mapping from AWS Marketplace SKU -> our product SKU. I attached an anonymized sample invoice for reference.
- Is there an entitlement object we can use to reconcile seats vs. metered units? Any examples of the fulfillment webhook payload would help the billing team.

Proposed next steps: a short call with procurement + engineering (30 min) so we can get the exact fields they require. Are you available next week?

Thanks,
Claire Dunn
Head of Partnerships, Aperture Analytics
[attachment: aperture-invoice-sample.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire@aperture.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace integration questions + sample invoice

Hi Claire — great to hear Aperture is moving forward.

Short answers up front:
- Metering: monthly usage will be reported to AWS Marketplace; final chargeability depends on whether you purchase via AWS (Marketplace fulfillment) or via RDC invoice. For Marketplace SaaS (metering), AWS bills the customer and remits to us.
- Entitlement: we emit an entitlement object that maps an AWS entitlement (SKU/Account) to a Redwood customer_id and product_id; that payload is what your finance team will use to reconcile.

I've attached our integration checklist and a proposed billing mapping template so procurement can fill required fields. For technical payloads, looping in Aditya (cc) — Aditya can share the webhook sample and signing guidance.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync on Tue 5/25 at 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Next items for us to provide before the call:
- Example fulfillment webhook (signed payload)
- Billing mapping template prefilled with one test SKU
- Link to DocuSign for the SaaS order form if you want to route via Redwood instead of Marketplace for yo ur first invoice

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-mp-integration-checklist.pdf (document)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace integration questions + sample invoice

Claire / Sergio — quick technical note ahead of the procurement call.

1) Fulfillment webhook: the webhook payload contains the entitlement_id, aws_account_id, sku_id, metered_units, and a timestamp. We sign the payload with an HMAC header (X-Redwood-Signature) so you can validate origin. Sample attached (redacted).

2) Entitlement vs. seats: our entitlement object can express either a prefixed-cumulative meter (consumption) or a seat count. For reconciliation you can map AWS SKU -> Redwood product_id -> Aperture SKU in the attached mapping template.

3) Billing routing options:
   - Marketplace-first: AWS invoices end customer; you reconcile on AWS invoice lines (recommended if you want consolidated AWS billing).
   - Direct Redwood invoice: we can do an off-marketplace purchase (DocuSign order form) and bill directly on our net terms. That simplifies entitlement mapping but sacrifices consolidated AWS billing.

See attached: webhook-sample.json (payload example). Happy to walk through fields on the call.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Integrations — Redwood Inference
[attachment: webhook-sample.json (snippet)]

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks for the PO and for clarifying procurement needs. Quick summary and answers: 

1) Invoicing cadence / who receives invoice
   - Marketplace purchase: AWS invoices Aperture directly; AWS remits to Redwood. Redwood will also emit a usage report (CSV) to your finance contact daily/weekly depending on volume — we can set daily exports for your GL team.
   - Direct Redwood invoice (off-marketplace): Redwood issues monthly invoices to Aperture via our billing system; net terms are 30 days by default (we can discuss 45d on the enterprise contract).

2) Reconciliation artifacts provided by Redwood
   - Usage report (CSV) with columns: entitlement_id, aws_account_id, sku_id, metered_units, unit_price, billed_amount, invoice_ref
   - Entitlement export (JSON) for matching to your internal SKU
   - Billing mapping spreadsheet (attached) prefilled with Aperture test SKU -> Redwood product id -> example AWS SKU

3) Next steps and operational handoff
   - I attached the billing-mapping-aperture.xlsx with example rows filled. Please confirm one test SKU that we can use during the sandbox cutover.
   - DocuSign (SaaS order form) is ready if you want Redwood to be the billed party: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc123
   - Proposed cutover week: 2027-06-07 (can be adjusted) — we recommend a sandbox 48-hour ingest window to validate webhook delivery and mapping.

Let me know if you want us to route contract through AWS marketplace listing (we'll coordinate listing activation) or run the first invoice off-marketplace via DocuSign so procurement can use your existing PO flow.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
